answer: Randomized audit slot assignment. Each identity is assigned audit slots derived from a verifiable random beacon published after registration, so attackers cannot precompute which identities will be sampled. A sampled identity must answer an interactive challenge within one pulse of the beacon; failure freezes it until a costly re-registration. Attackers can only flood identities whose future slot is knowable, forcing them to pay a fresh anchor cost per identity surfaced by the unpredictable river of beacon outputs.
